every sub-question verbatim from the question paper (text layer read
page-by-page with pdftotext -layout, figures verified against rendered
page images), memo answers verbatim from the official Marking Guidelines.
Figures are described in [FIGURE: ...] brackets inside 'context'.
FORMAT (same as 2024): P1 is Climate & Weather (Q1), Geomorphology (Q2)
plus Section B mapwork (Q3, 1:50 000 topographical map 3318DD STELLENBOSCH
The physical map sheets are separate and not in this repo, so map-read
inputs for calculations come from the memo's accepted values.
MEMO ANOMALY (same as 2024): page 3 of the marking-guidelines PDF is a
marking-principles demonstration (a sample marked script from a different
paper - e.g. it shows '1.1.1 A (South Atlantic High)'). It is NOT the
answer key for this paper; the real answers start on memo page 4

questions.context: 1.3 Refer to the sketches below on the mid-latitude cyclone. [FIGURE: Four panels. questions.context: 1.4 Refer to the infographic below on Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi. A: FACT FILE - 'Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi was first observed off the north-east coast of Madagascar. C: SATELLITE IMAGE, time span 2025/01/08 03:30 to 2025/01/08 14:00 UTC - loosely organised spiralling cloud mass east of Madagascar, no clear eye. D: SATELLITE IMAGE, time span 2025/01/13 14:00 to 2025/01/13 15:30 UTC - well-developed circular cyclone with a distinct dark eye in the Mozambique Channel west of Madagascar; a dashed curve marks the 'Forward left-hand quadrant'. questions.context: 2.5 Refer to the extract and photograph below on catchment and river management. IMPACT OF SETTLEMENTS ON RIVER MANAGEMENT: 'Dense settlements that locate along rivers have a negative impact on rivers. The main reason is that these settlements generally receive poor service provision. These poor communities also do not have the means to pay for the provision of services, such as waste removal. When large amounts of waste pile up in the settlement, the community is more likely to dispose of the waste in the river. This leads to further pollution, eventually leading to serious health risks for the community.' [FIGURE (adapted from https://witsvuvuzela.com/2022/11/28/-residents-live-on-the-edge-of-a-health-hazard/): Photograph of an informal settlement with shacks built right up to the eroded banks on both sides of a river; the channel and banks are strewn with litter and solid waste.]

questions.context: SECTION B, QUESTION 3: GEOGRAPHICAL SKILLS AND TECHNIQUES. GENERAL INFORMATION ON STELLENBOSCH: [FIGURE: outline map of South Africa's provinces with Stellenbosch marked by a dot in the south-west (Western Cape); north arrow.] Coordinates: 33°45'S; 18°45'E. 'Stellenbosch is located in a hilly, sheltered valley within the Cape Winelands, with an average elevation of 136 metres above sea level, surrounded by hills and mountains, like Papegaaiberg, Stellenboschberg, and the Jonkershoek, Drakenstein and Simonsberg mountain ranges. It is situated approximately 50 kilometres east of Cape Town. Stellenbosch has a Mediterranean climate with warm, dry summers and cool, rainy winters. The Eerste River originates in the Jonkershoek Mountains, 60 kilometres east of Cape Town, and flows through the Jonkershoek Valley before reaching Stellenbosch.' [Adapted from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch]. English/Afrikaans terms on the topographical map: River/Rivier; Nature reserve/Natuurreservaart; Mountain/Berg.
